Quick tutorials

Tutorial 1 · All prime families · 301+ · 394 = 197 × 2
In All prime families · 301+, enter 197 for Prime and 2 for Multiplier, then choose Build prime × multiplier. When the new prime-family character is generated, click Export this .sprite3 to download it. Import the downloaded .sprite3 into Scratch, then use a 2–307 times-family example to inspect its face + arms + legs; create your own face, create/import your own limbs, and add the Numberling.

Tutorial 2 · Rectangle form · 352 = 16 × 22
Choose a band that has rectangle forms. For this example, choose Band 36 (351–360), open 352, and use its 16 × 22 rectangle form. Then click Export this .sprite3 to download the generated sprite. Open the downloaded .sprite3 in Scratch and add your own face, limbs, and Numberling.

Tutorial 3 · Download .sprite3, then add your own face, limbs & Numberling
First build or open the number you want, then click Export this .sprite3 to download it. Import that .sprite3 into Scratch. Use the number search and type basaperial, 36 to find Band 36 (351–360) as an example. basaperial, 36 is only the search text for the band. After importing your downloaded sprite, add your own face, limbs, and Numberling in Scratch.

Prime-family face & limb examples · 2–307

Use supplied Aperial characters from 2–307 as face/limb references for ×1, ×2, ×3 … ×10 and beyond. These are examples only: inspect the supplied character’s face and limbs. New 301+ characters should use your own face and your own/adjusted limbs, not automatically copied parts.

Example: 222 = 6 × 37. Open 222 to inspect its actual face + arm/leg setup as the ×6 reference. Then make a different face and adjust limbs for the new character.

Factor-Pair Source Animation & Sound References · 301+

For composite Aperials from 301 onward, choose a factor pair and inspect the REAL supplied source characters for both factors. Use their existing costumes, scripts, limbs, faces and sounds as references. This tool does not invent or recreate missing artwork, animation or audio. Supplied/official character material always takes priority.

Example: 360 = 18 × 20. Use the real supplied 18 and 20 sound and animation references.

Open a composite number from 301 onward to inspect its factor-pair references.

Body and animation editor

Factors and body dimensions are separate. Choose source colours or your own checkerboard. Open / Build restores supplied artwork.

What is preserved and what remains a draft

Prime-family face/limb examples use supplied references from 2–307. Seven saved Band 32 composite sprites are also included. Band 32 excludes 311, 313 and 317. The later saved 316 Camite and 319 Restored sprites take priority over earlier drafts. These saved drafts are not newly certified official designs.

Source SVG costumes, accessories, glyphs, costume sequences, motion blocks and sound names are preserved in source exports. Host show/hide broadcasts are adapted for band playback. The preview shows source costume order; verify full native motion and audio tails in Scratch. Source anomalies in costume reset names remain for review.

312 retains its supplied 12-column × 26-row body, 156 gold #ffd988 and 156 green #85e678 cells, with gold at bottom-left. Animated source poses retain their lighter glow colours. Body drafts alternate every individual cell horizontally and vertically. 312’s palette is not generalized to other numbers. Animated drafts use selected source face, arm and leg cutouts. Each track follows source costume timing; inspect cutouts before sharing. New drafts are silent.

Reference audio is compact 64 kbps Opus here, decoded to PCM WAV on export. Full source sound lengths, names and trigger blocks are retained. Browser preview lasts 6.4 seconds; longer source tails may continue in Scratch. This is compressed reference audio, not an exact original-WAV-byte copy or newly verified arrangement. Export reference band is a reference-based export, not a byte-identical original SB3.

Closest factors are mathematical suggestions, not a complete design rule. Import actual corrected sprites to replace drafts. SVG imports are single drawings with no animation or sound. Imported art and reviews last until the page closes; export your project. Credit the original creators.
